items.title: Entering the Gate, and Finding Real Delight in the Path Itself

items.zh: 趣入者，謂得淨信增上力故，或有在家遠離惡行，受持學處；或趣非家遠離諸欲，受持學處。
items.en: Entry: through the strengthening power of pure confidence, some, remaining householders, distance themselves from wrongdoing and undertake the relevant precepts; others go forth from household life, distancing themselves from sensual desire, and undertake the relevant precepts.

items.zh: 攝樂者，謂依出離眾苦行迹，及依遠離欲樂、自苦二邊行迹，於佛善說法毘奈耶真實聖教深生愛樂。
items.en: Delighting attraction: resting on the path that leads out of every suffering, and on the path that avoids both indulgence in sensual pleasure and self-inflicted asceticism, one comes to deeply delight in the Buddha's true teaching of doctrine and discipline.

items.title: The Very First Arousal of the Resolve for Awakening, and What Follows After

items.zh: 初發處者，謂即最初於可厭法深生厭離；於能成辦真實理義，如實了知有勝功德，而創趣入。名初發處。
items.en: The point of initial arousal: it is when one first develops deep aversion towards what genuinely deserves aversion, and, truly recognising the excellent virtue of what genuinely accomplishes real, ultimate meaning, newly enters upon it for the very first time. This is called the point of initial arousal.

items.zh: 非初發處者，謂已趣入補特伽羅，現成熟時，常不捨離諸佛菩薩，諸明了處轉轉明了。由此成熟，轉轉增進。
items.en: What is not the point of initial arousal: when one who has already entered the path is presently ripening, never departing from the buddhas and bodhisattvas, and each field of knowledge grows progressively clearer — through this ripening, one continues progressively advancing.

items.title: The Slow Path and the Fast Path to Purification, and Precepts Kept Out of Fear

items.zh: 遠清淨者，謂由懈怠，或由違緣，經極長時，或經多生、或經多劫方能清淨。近清淨者，當知一切與此相違。
items.en: Distant purification: because of laziness, or because of unfavorable conditions, purification is reached only after an extremely long time, across many lifetimes or many eons. Near purification: it should be understood as entirely the reverse of this.

items.zh: 加行者，謂為獲得自勝義利，猛利樂欲為所依故；或怖當來墮諸惡趣，或怖現法他所譏毀，於諸學處常勤護持；無間所作、殷重所作。
items.en: Application: in order to attain one's own excellent, ultimate benefit, resting on intense aspiration, and fearing future rebirth in the lower realms or present criticism from others, one constantly and diligently guards the relevant precepts — acting without interruption, and acting with genuine earnestness.

items.title: Section: The Inner Aspiration That Powers Practice, and Two Kinds of Giving

items.zh: 意樂者，謂於諸法正觀察忍為所依故，於佛善說法毘奈耶不可引奪，於他所證深生信解。信有功德為所依故，於三寶所及於獲得自義利所深信無動。
items.en: Aspiration: resting on a settled acceptance reached through correctly examining all phenomena, one's confidence in the Buddha's true teaching of doctrine and discipline cannot be shaken by anyone, and one deeply trusts what others have genuinely realised. Resting on confidence in genuine virtue, one's trust in the Three Jewels, and in attaining one's own ultimate benefit, remains unshakeable.

items.zh: 財攝受者，謂於一切飲食等物有匱乏者，施與一切飲食等物；或於隨順飲食等物有匱乏者，施與隨順飲食等物。法攝受者，謂或宣說正法，施諸有情；或開顯正義，施諸有情。
items.en: Attraction through wealth: giving food and other necessities to those who lack them; or giving money and similar means to those who lack what would let them obtain such necessities. Attraction through teaching: expounding the true Dharma to beings, or revealing its genuine meaning to them.

items.title: Section: Miracles That Inspire Confidence, and Teaching Hidden or Made Fully Explicit

items.zh: 神通引攝者，謂具神通者，哀愍有情故，或為有情意樂清淨、或為有情加行清淨增上力故，示現種種神通變化。欲令有情見已、聞已，於佛聖教，或當獲得意樂清淨，或當修行無倒加行。彼諸有情，由此神變引攝心故，或有獲得意樂清淨，或有修行無倒加行。宣說正法者，謂於獲得自勝義利若無堪能，為說正法，伴助令彼發生正行；若有堪能，為說正法，隨順令彼速證通慧。
items.en: Guidance through miraculous power: one possessing miraculous ability, out of compassion for beings ... displays various miraculous transformations. ... Explicit teaching of the true Dharma: for one not yet capable of attaining their own ultimate benefit, teaching the true Dharma accompanies and supports them in developing correct conduct; for one already capable, teaching the true Dharma guides them swiftly towards realising penetrating wisdom.

items.zh: 隱密說法者，謂於嬰兒智慧有情，隱覆廣大甚深義法，為說麁淺易可悟入、易為方便趣入處法。顯了說法者，謂於廣大智慧有情，已善悟入聖教理者，為其開示廣大甚深道理處法。
items.en: Teaching through hidden meaning: for beings of "infant" wisdom, the vast and profound teaching is deliberately held back, and a coarser, simpler teaching is given instead, one more readily entered ... Teaching made fully explicit: for beings of vast wisdom who have already skilfully entered the true meaning of the noble teaching, the vast and profound doctrine itself is opened and revealed to them directly.

items.zh: 下品加行者，謂若遠離無間加行及殷重加行。中品加行者，謂或遠離無間加行，或復遠離殷重加行，於二加行隨闕一種。

items.title: Three Grades of Effort, and the Classical Path of Hearing, Reflection, and Cultivation

items.zh: 上品加行者，謂無間加行及殷重加行二俱相應。聽聞者，謂於佛語深生信解，精勤聽聞、受持、讀誦契經等法。思惟者，謂居遠離，樂思惟法，推度其義，解了決定。
items.en: Superior application: both uninterrupted effort and earnest effort are present together. ... Hearing: with deep trust in the Buddha's own words, diligently listening to, retaining, and reciting the scriptures and other teachings. Reflection: dwelling apart in solitude, delighting in reflecting on the teaching, examining its meaning, until genuine understanding and settled conviction are reached.

items.zh: 修習者，謂於止、舉、捨相正審觀察為先，深心欣樂修止、舉、捨。
items.en: Cultivation: first correctly and carefully observing the marks of stillness, uplifting, and equanimity, then cultivating stillness, uplifting, and equanimity with genuine, heartfelt delight.

items.title: Section: Taking On Students — Serving Without Attachment, and the Five-Fold Way to Resolve Regret

items.zh: 攝受者，謂無染心，以親教師及軌範師道理方便，無有顛倒與作依止。又即於彼發起種種別供事行。謂看病行，給施如法衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥資生具行，除遣憂愁及惡作行，除遣煩惱、隨煩惱行。
items.en: Embracing: with a mind free of self-interested attachment, serving, correctly and without distortion, as a student's preceptor and instructor in discipline and meditation. One further undertakes specific acts of care on their behalf — nursing them when ill, providing proper clothing, food, bedding, and medicine, resolving their grief and regret, and helping dissolve their afflictions and secondary afflictions.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知皆名別供事行。

items.title: Section: Subduing Difficult Students — Three Graded Responses, Always Rooted in Compassion

items.zh: 降伏者，謂深防護自身雜染。於毀犯者，若犯下品，慈心諫誨；若犯中品，慈心訶罰；若犯上品，慈心驅擯。
items.en: Subduing: deeply guarding against defilement in oneself first. Towards one who has broken discipline: if the offence is of the lower grade, correcting them with a compassionate mind through gentle counsel; if of the middle grade, rebuking them with a compassionate mind; if of the upper grade, expelling them with a compassionate mind.

items.zh: 當知此中，諫誨、訶罰，令彼及餘利益安樂。
驅擯一種，若重攝受，令彼及餘利益安樂。若驅擯已，不重攝受，但令其餘利益安樂。何以故？餘若見彼毀犯因緣，既被驅擯，便自防護，不起毀犯故。
items.en: As for expulsion specifically: if the offender is later welcomed back, this benefits both them and the rest of the community; if they are not welcomed back after expulsion, this still benefits the rest of the community. Why is this? Because others, seeing that the offence led to genuine expulsion, are moved to guard themselves and avoid committing the same offence.

blocks.text: The means of ripening, one by one. They read like a handbook for anyone who teaches.

"Through pure confidence, some remain householders and take precepts; others go forth." Delight: "resting on the path that avoids both indulgence and self-mortification, one comes to delight deeply in the Buddha's teaching".
"When one first develops deep aversion towards what deserves aversion, and recognises the virtue of what accomplishes real meaning."
"Because of laziness or unfavourable conditions, purification is reached only after many lifetimes or aeons"; or near, in this life.
"Fearing future rebirth in the lower realms or present criticism, one guards the precepts." Aspiration: "confidence in the Buddha's teaching that cannot be shaken by anyone".

"Giving food and necessities to those who lack them." Master Cháng Bǎi: wealth only relieves urgent need; the Dharma helps for good. Miracles inspire confidence; teaching supports those not yet capable.
"For beings of 'infant' wisdom, the profound teaching is held back, and a simpler one given"; for the mature, "made fully explicit".
Superior effort is both continuous and earnest. Hearing, reflecting, and cultivating: "first observing the marks of stillness, uplifting, and equanimity".

"With a mind free of self-interest, serving as a student's preceptor and instructor." Towards one who breaks discipline: a minor offence, gentle counsel; moderate, rebuke; grave, expulsion, "always rooted in compassion". "If the expelled is later welcomed back, both benefit; if not, the community still benefits."

quiz.q: Delighting attraction rests on "the path avoiding both sensual indulgence and self-torment." What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: self-torment like outsiders baking in the sun or standing on one leg; Miào Jìng: the middle way is the four foundations, the eightfold path
quiz.why: "Resting on the path that avoids both indulgence in sensual pleasure and self-inflicted asceticism, one comes to deeply delight in the Buddha's true teaching." Master Cháng Bǎi: like outsiders baking in the sun or standing on one leg, thinking suffering now ends suffering. Venerable Miào Jìng: practising the middle way is the four foundations of mindfulness — the eightfold path.

quiz.q: "The point of initial arousal" — the note reads it as first arousing bodhicitta. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: the moment of first attaining the path and acceptance of non-arising; Cháng Bǎi: pushing away worldly attachment, pulled by supramundane virtue
quiz.why: "It is when one first develops deep aversion towards what genuinely deserves aversion, and, truly recognising the excellent virtue of what accomplishes ultimate meaning, newly enters upon it." Venerable Miào Jìng: the moment of first attaining the noble path and acceptance of non-arising is the point of initial arousal. Master Cháng Bǎi: the push is pushing away attachment to worldly things; the pull is supramundane virtue drawing one onward.

quiz.q: Distant and near purification — where does Master Cháng Bǎi draw the line?
options: before the path of preparation is distant; attaining non-discriminating wisdom is near
quiz.why: "Distant purification: because of laziness, or because of unfavorable conditions, purification is reached only after an extremely long time … Near purification: entirely the reverse." Master Cháng Bǎi: in other words, everything before the path of preparation is distant purification; only attaining non-discriminating wisdom is near purification.

quiz.q: "Attraction through wealth: giving necessities to those lacking." What's its limit, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: wealth only meets urgent need — it isn't ultimate
quiz.why: "Attraction through wealth: giving food and other necessities to those who lack them." Master Cháng Bǎi: because wealth can only relieve urgent need — it can't be ultimate.

quiz.q: "Attraction through teaching." Why is it more ultimate, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: every problem comes from this one mind
quiz.why: "Attraction through teaching: expounding the true Dharma to beings, or revealing its genuine meaning to them." Master Cháng Bǎi: attraction through teaching is more ultimate than through wealth, because every problem comes from this one mind.

quiz.q: "Teaching through hidden meaning, for beings of infant wisdom." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: the person's wisdom is like an infant's
quiz.why: "Teaching through hidden meaning: for beings of 'infant' wisdom, the vast and profound teaching is deliberately held back, and a coarser, simpler teaching is given instead." Venerable Miào Jìng: it means this person's wisdom is like an infant's.

quiz.q: Subduing offenders "minor, moderate, serious." How do the lectures grade offenses?
options: Miào Jìng by state of mind: overcome by affliction is middling; Cháng Bǎi: subtle or ignorant offenses are minor — gently counseled
quiz.why: "Towards one who has broken discipline: if the offence is minor, correcting them with a compassionate mind through gentle counsel; if moderate, rebuking them; if serious, expelling them." Venerable Miào Jìng: when affliction comes and can't be subdued and one follows it — that offence is middling. Master Cháng Bǎi: a minor offence, subtle or committed in ignorance, should be met with compassionate counsel. The lectures grade by the offender's mind; the English only by severity.
